acceptance_checks: Migration mode is entered only with BOTH the <!-- shiki:migration --> marker and the mergegate:migration label; the marker alone blocks with the label message.
The migration is resolved and executed from the BASE branch's registry, and a PR that carries its own new migration definition blocks because the id is absent from base.
A conforming PR whose .shiki diff equals the re-run output exactly passes.
An extra changed file, a missing produced file, and a single changed byte each block with a reason naming the path — one case per shape.
A missing Migration: line, more than one such line, an id absent from the base registry, an already-applied migration, and a destructive migration each block with a distinct reason.
tests/test_migration_mode.py drives the gate for every case above.
scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh covers the self-defining-migration attempt and a one-byte deviation.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
The migration function is resolved and executed from the BASE branch via git inside mergegate_check.py; no new workflow flag is added and the base .shiki snapshot is not relied on for scripts/.
non_goals: Resolving the migration from the PR head's registry
Allowing any non-.shiki file in a migration-mode PR
Allowing a destructive or already-applied migration
Changing contract, goal_reconcile, amendment, post_merge_reconcile, closeout or normal-path handling
Touching any file outside the declared locks
scope:
In `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, add a `migration` mode entered only when BOTH the `<!-- shiki:migration -->` marker is in the PR body AND the maintainer-applied `mergegate:migration` label is present — the same two-factor shape `contract_decision` implements, with the same message when the label is missing. The PR body must also declare the migration id on its own line as `Migration: <id>`.

The rule is a re-run proof. Given the base `.shiki` snapshot the gate already reconstructs for other modes, apply the declared migration — resolved from the BASE branch's registry, never the PR head's — to a copy of that snapshot, and require the result to equal the PR head's `.shiki` exactly, file for file and byte for byte. Any file present in one and not the other, and any byte difference, is a blocking reason naming the path. Block, with a distinct reason each, when: the declared id is absent from the base registry; the id line is missing or names more than one migration; the migration is already recorded as applied in the base `.shiki/migrations/state.json`; the migration is `destructive`; or any changed file is outside `.shiki/`.

The base-registry requirement is the security property and must be implemented as such: the migration function is resolved and executed from the base branch's `scripts/shiki_migrations.py`, so a PR cannot define the migration whose output it is measured against. Note this explicitly in the code comment, because a future reader will otherwise be tempted to simplify it to the head registry.

Add `tests/test_migration_mode.py` driving the real gate: a conforming PR passes; a PR with one extra changed file blocks naming that path; a PR with one byte changed in one file blocks naming that path; a PR missing a file the migration produces blocks; a declared id absent from the base registry blocks; a missing or duplicated `Migration:` line blocks; an already-applied migration blocks; a destructive migration blocks; a non-.shiki file blocks; the marker without the label blocks with the label message; and — the case that matters most — a PR that carries its own new migration definition and declares it does NOT pass, because the id is absent from the base registry. Add adversarial cases to `scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh` for the self-defining-migration attempt and for a one-byte deviation.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a change that must touch every record in the mirror cannot be delivered at all. Declaring `path:.shiki/tasks/**` in the task's locks does not help, because `enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations` rejects a foreign task file independently of locks: `elif path != task_file: blocking.append('PR changes unrelated Shiki task file ...')`.
  Measured: 104 of 112 task files lack `cca_checklist_profile`; the promotion task that wanted to require it (T-20260729T065622764296Z-48021407) could not backfill them and needed two Spec Amendments to drop the criterion.
  Root cause: every existing deny-by-default mode is scoped to ONE goal's records — contract, goal_reconcile, amendment — because every existing mode models a goal-shaped change. A repository-wide change has no goal.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: a two-factor mode whose entire proof obligation is that the diff equals the re-run output of a migration registered on the BASE branch.
  Why the base registry and not the head: running a head-supplied migration function against base data proves nothing — a PR could define a migration that emits exactly the diff it wants, and the check would pass. Resolving from base means the gate executes code the base branch already merged. This is the whole security argument for the mode and the single thing a future simplification must not break.
  Reproducible when: a conforming PR passes, a one-byte deviation blocks naming the file, and a PR carrying its own migration definition blocks because the id is not on base.

SCOPE AMENDMENT (2026-08-05) — MANDATED IMPLEMENTATION PATH. Resolve and execute the declared migration by importing `subprocess` INSIDE `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, reading the base ref from `pr['baseRefName']`, and relying on the checkout's `fetch-depth: 0` together with the existing `git fetch origin "$base_ref"` (shiki-mergegate.yml:48). Measured: the `--base-shiki` snapshot is `.shiki`-only (`shiki-mergegate.yml:76` archives only `.shiki`), and `mergegate_check.py`'s imports are `annotations, argparse, dataclass, json, re, sys, pathlib.Path, typing.Any` plus eight `shiki_*` modules — no `subprocess`, no `os` — so the base branch's `scripts/` is unreachable as the contract originally assumed. Do NOT add a new workflow flag or archive base `scripts/`: that path needs four files outside these locks. The security property is unchanged and remains load-bearing: the migration function MUST be read from the BASE branch, never from the PR head, so a PR cannot define the migration whose output it is measured against.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Enforce a migration mode whose diff must equal a registered migration's output
